title: Cross-team leaders huddle - operational pulse and rollouts
body:
Meeting: Cross-team engineering leadership huddle
Date: 2026-04-01 09:30 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-leadership
Attendees: Aisha (host), Liam, Sofia, Daniel, Priya, Rana (brief), PM reps: Elena, Marcus (partial)

Goals: quick sync on operational health, active rollouts, unresolved cross-team blockers, and short decision window for canary tuning. Keep to 45m.

Agenda:
1) Operational metrics & incidents (10m)
2) Serving runtime canary rollout update (10m)
3) Dedicated capacity contract handoff (5m)
4) Private deployment support ramp (5m)
5) Cross-team blockers / escalation list (10m)
6) Action items + parking lot (5m)

Notes:
1) Operational metrics & incidents
- SLOs: p50 generation latency up ~12% week-over-week for hosted-api routes  /v1/generate; p95 stable. Root cause suspected: a small spike in long-context requests + increased kv-cache misses after recent kernel change.
- Error budget: hosted-api error budget at 94.8% (still green). We saw 3 brief 5xx spikes on 2026-03-31 between 03:40-04:10 PT correlated with GPU OOM on shard-gp11. SRE runbook executed; auto-fallback to lower-capacity variant worked.
- Action taken: rollback of kernel selection tweak on canary nodes (PR 918) until perf regression fully reproduced in perf lab. Liam to coordinate perf repro.

2) Serving runtime canary rollout
- Current canary: 15% traffic on region-us-west for v2-runtime (quantization improvements). Early signs: token throughput lower for batch sizes <4. Hypothesis: batching heuristic needs tuning for mixed-length workloads.
- Decision: pause incremental traffic bump to 25% until batching heuristic is tuned. Sofia to own tuning work; target interim patch by 2026-04-05.
- Notes: preserve KV cache compatibility across variants; update canary policy doc (linked).

3) Dedicated capacity (sales handoff)
- Contract for customer X (3 clusters reserved) requires 99.95% monthly uptime SLA and a dedicated cross-region failover plan. Ops checklist reviewed.
- Gap noted: automated cost attribution per-route not wired into billing export yet (product ask). Daniel to scope a 2-sprint delivery plan and present to GTM.

4) Private deployment support ramp
- Support readiness: runbooks for VPC private control plane need clearer guidance on KMS rotations and customer audit logs. Priya will own a one-page runbook for QuickStart by 2026-04-08.
- On-prem package: engineering needs to confirm hardware minimums for 8-bit quantized models at 2k context. Marcus to share bench numbers next sync.

5) Cross-team blockers / escalations
- Blocker: rollout gating for routing policies depends on RBAC work in console (PLAT-217). Blocker status: Console team needs 2 more sprints. Workaround: manual policy injection via API for critical customers. Owner: Elena to triage.
- Blocker: tracing hooks integration with third-party APM has intermittent sampling gaps. SRE to add higher-fidelity traces for the next 72h.

6) Action items (owner — due)
- Liam: reproduce perf regression for kernel selection in perf lab and report a root-cause hypothesis (2026-04-03).
- Sofia: implement batching-heuristic patch and run perf sweep, prepare rollback plan (2026-04-05).
- Daniel: scope billing export + attribution tickets and present sprint plan to GTM (2026-04-06).
- Priya: publish Private QuickStart runbook focusing on KMS rotation and audit logs (2026-04-08).
- Elena: enable manual routing-policy injection for three enterprise customers as temporary mitigation and document the process (2026-04-04).

Parking lot / Notes-to-self:
- Revisit model variant fallback thresholds after batch-heuristic fix.
- Consider increasing canary region diversity for future rollouts.
- Need a short owner for release-automation infra that bridges release-engineering and serving-runtime (small role suggestion: 10% allocation).

Decisions made:
- Pause traffic ramp for v2-runtime canary until batching fix shipped.
- Maintain current hosted-api SLO but increase monitoring on token throughput distribution.

Open questions:
- Should we fast-track a hotfix for kernel selection to only affect long-context cases? (yes/no) — follow-up: Liam to propose fix design.
- Is the temporary manual routing-policy injection sustainable beyond 3 weeks? (Elena to assess).

Next meeting: 2026-04-08 09:30 PT.

Quick standup log (raw) — captured between leaders for the week
- Aisha: prioritized canary pause, aligning PM/infra.
- Liam: perf lab repro in progress.
- Sofia: batching patch prototype ready tomorrow.
- Daniel: billing export scoping started; need input from finance.
- Priya: runbook draft started; will include sample KMS rotation command snippets.

Slack refs / Jira quick links:
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime \"canary perf blip\" (link: slack://channel?team=redwood&id=eng-runtime)
- JIRA tickets: ENG-3421 (kernel perf), PLAT-217 (console RBAC), DED-121 (customer X contract), PRIV-88 (private runbooks)

Summary: Short meeting; main outcome is to pause canary ramp and focus on a batching fix to address p50 regressions. Action owners assigned with near-term due dates. We will re-evaluate next week with perf data.

Document notes: rough working doc; will tidy and move to Confluence if needed for long-term tracking.
